baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Layered historical traditions and critical reconstruction of ancient documents (1923–1936)
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Richter describes Gu’s text criticism and recovery of earlier Chinese critics; Lu’s abstract analyzes the distinction between original records and later transmission. The target is the cross-tradition field Critical historical scholarship, not a claim of dependence on Ranke.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Ancient unity questioned and the Chinese nation reformulated: a contested trajectory (1923–1939)
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Richter describes Gu’s early challenge to a unitary ancient origin. Zheng reads the 1939 unity thesis critically; Jenco’s abstract emphasizes a politically open, plural community, while Kim’s emphasizes retreat toward homogenization. These disagreements remain explicit; no single retrospective verdict is adopted.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Li Ji and Liang Yuantong object that antiquity-doubting must move beyond documents to their social conditions, as Dirlik reports
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Dirlik’s epilogue, p. 265, reports these Marxist historians’ methodological criticism. Their original texts are unread. The named objection is routed through Marxist historiography, not equated with a consensus of that whole field.
